Japan · Fish & colourful greens

Sesame salmon rice bowl

Sesame salmon, brown rice and colourful vegetables. About 25 minutes with ready-cooked rice and an air fryer.

  • ⏱ ~25 min · ready rice
  • 🍽 2 portions
  • 🔥 670 kcal / portion*
Cook step by step →

Ingredients

Makes 2 portions

  • 420 gcooked brown rice (ready-cooked pouch or safely chilled rice)
  • 260 graw salmon fillets (about 130 g each; thawed, boneless)
  • 300 gbroccoli
  • 200 gcucumber
  • 150 gcarrots
  • 5 mlrapeseed oil
  • 15 mlreduced-salt soy sauce
  • 15 mlrice vinegar
  • 10 gtoasted sesame seeds
  • 10 gfresh ginger

Before you start

Equipment

Air fryer or oven; steamer or saucepan; microwave or saucepan for rice; board, knife and grater. Clean fish tweezers if any pin bones remain.

Allergens

Fish, soy, sesame; wheat if present in soy sauce.

Make it yours

Use firm tofu for a fish-free version; check soy and sesame allergies. Nutrition will change with substitutions.

Method

  1. Choose your rice

    Ready-cooked pouchDefault

    • Keep the ready-cooked rice pouch unopened until step 7.
    • Cooking for later? Store salmon and vegetables separately; heat rice only when serving.

    Chilled rice

    • Use rice cooled promptly, refrigerated and cooked within the last 24 hours. It must not have been reheated.
    • Keep chilled until step 7. Reheat once and eat now.

    Fresh rice

    • Start with about 70 g dry rice per portion. Rinse; follow the packet’s water ratio and cooking time.
    • Weigh out 210 g cooked rice per portion. Cool any extra promptly.
    • Allow about 55–65 minutes for the meal; cook the salmon near the end.

    Rice cooker

    • Rinse rice. Use your cooker’s cup, brown-rice water guide and minimum batch size.
    • Run the full cycle and rest. Fluff; weigh out 210 g cooked rice per portion.
    • Allow extra time for the cooker cycle. Cool spare rice promptly.
    What it should look likeReady-cooked rice, ready to heat.

  2. Prepare the vegetables

    • Wash produce. Cut broccoli into 3 cm florets and carrots into 3 mm slices.
    • Slice cucumber into half-moons; keep it chilled separately.
    What it should look likeEven broccoli and carrot pieces; cucumber kept separate.

  3. Mix the ginger dressing

    • Peel ginger with a spoon, then finely grate it. Keep fingertips away from the grater.
    • Mix with all the soy sauce and rice vinegar. Keep this dressing away from raw fish.
    What it should look likeA thin dressing with fine ginger shreds.

  4. Prepare the salmon

    • Keep the fillets whole and skin-on. Pat dry with kitchen paper; feel along the flesh for pin bones.
    • Pull any bones out with clean fish tweezers, in the direction they point. Brush with the measured oil.
    • Keep dressing and sesame for serving. Wash hands and clean raw-fish tools.
    What it should look likeWhole fillets, no remaining pin bones, lightly coated with oil.

  5. Cook the salmon

    Air fryerDefault

    • Set the air fryer to 200°C; preheat only if your manual requires it.
    • Place fillets skin-side down, spaced apart. Cook 8–10 minutes; start checking at 8 minutes.
    • While it cooks, continue with vegetables and rice. Use more batches if crowded.

    Oven

    • Heat oven to 180°C (160°C fan). Place oiled salmon skin-side down on a lined tray.
    • Bake 10–15 minutes; thicker fillets may need longer. Check from 10 minutes.
    • Cook vegetables and heat rice meanwhile. Allow about 30 minutes for the full bowl.
    What it should look likeThickest part: steaming hot, opaque and flakes easily. If translucent or cool, cook longer and check again.

  6. Cook the vegetables

    SteamDefault

    • Use broccoli and carrots already cut in step 2. Put in a basket above boiling water; cover.
    • Steam 5–7 minutes; check from 5 minutes. Remove tender pieces first and drain.
    • Keep water in the pot. Open the lid away from your face.

    Boil

    • Add prepared carrots to boiling water. Once boiling again, cook 2 minutes.
    • Add broccoli. Once gently boiling again, cook 4–5 minutes.
    • Fork-check both vegetables, then drain carefully.
    What it should look likeA fork enters carrot and broccoli stems with gentle resistance.

  7. Heat the rice

    MicrowaveDefault

    • Heat ready-cooked pouch rice following its packet. Serve freshly cooked rice as it is.
    • For chilled rice: cover with a vent and a splash of water. Microwave in short bursts, stirring until steaming throughout.
    • Reheat rice once only and eat now. For meal prep, leave pouches unopened and follow Meal prep.

    Stovetop

    • For a pouch, follow its stovetop directions. For chilled rice, add a splash of water to a saucepan and cover.
    • Warm gently, stirring until steaming throughout. Freshly cooked hot rice needs no reheating.
    • Reheat rice once only and eat now. For meal prep, leave pouches unopened and follow Meal prep.
    What it should look likeSteaming-hot rice throughout; no cold pockets.

  8. Build your bowls

    • Divide rice, salmon, broccoli and carrots between bowls. Add cucumber.
    • Drizzle with the clean ginger dressing and sprinkle over all the sesame.
    • Eating later? Keep components separate and follow Meal prep.
    What it should look likeSalmon over rice, colourful vegetables alongside, sesame on top.

Meal prep and storage

Choose a rice route

For future meals, keep rice pouches unopened until serving, or cook fresh rice. Previously chilled rice reheated today is for eating now.

Cool & store

Cool salmon and vegetables in shallow containers; refrigerate within 2 hours at 4°C or below. Cool fresh rice ideally within 1 hour; use within 24 hours. Freeze portions for later promptly.

Keep toppings separate

Pack cucumber, clean dressing and sesame separately. Plan to eat chilled salmon and vegetables the next day. Store unopened rice pouches as their label directs.

Reheat & finish

Thaw frozen portions in the fridge. Reheat only once until steaming throughout. Heat pouch rice when serving; add cold toppings afterwards. Transport chilled food with an ice pack.
